hub.title: POSITIONS & ROLES
hub.intro: In indoor volleyball, positions are numbered P1 to P6 counter-clockwise as seen from behind your own court. Rotation happens clockwise on every side-out. The number of players and tactical systems differ by format — pick the one that matches your practice.

6v6.description: 6 players + libero, 9×18 m court, 2.43 m net. Systems 5-1, 4-2, 6-2 with clockwise rotation.

5v5.description: Transition between 4v4 and 6v6. No libero. Pentagon, 3F/2B, 2F/3B configurations depending on the chosen placement.

4v4.description: Reduced court, 2 front + 2 back. Diamond, Box, 3-1 line formations with penetrating setter.

page.subtitle: Positions and tactical systems for {{label}} volleyball.

crossLink.html: Check the <link>Positioning and defense</link> guide to see how this configuration places itself depending on the opposing attack zone.

6.tagline: Official FIVB / FFVolley format: 6 players + libero, 9×18 m court, 3 m attack line, 2.43 m net (M) / 2.24 m (W).
6.rules: Zones numbered counter-clockwise from behind your own court (Z1 = server). Clockwise rotation on side-out (Z2→Z1→Z6→Z5→Z4→Z3→Z2). Rule 7.4: at the moment of serve contact, positions are controlled by the feet (Z2 closer to the net than Z1, etc.). Block of 1, 2 or 3. The libero replaces back-row players without counting as a substitution.

5.tagline: Hybrid format, not officially FIVB/FFVb sanctioned. Used in schools, intramurals, fill-ins and as a transition between 4v4 and 6v6.
5.rules: 2+3 (penetrating setter recommended) or 3+2 (fixed front setter). No libero. Adapted overlap rule: Z4>Z5, Z3>Z6, Z2>Z1 (3-2 setup) or partial relations (2-3). Defensive recommendations are logical adaptations of 6v6, not a codified regulation.

4.tagline: No official FIVB regulation. Played in US university intramurals, recreational tournaments, educational transition (FFVb, Volleyball Canada).
4.rules: 9×9 m court (sometimes reduced), 3 touches, blocking allowed, clockwise rotation. 2 front + 2 back at every rotation. Common formations: diamond (1-2-1 center setter), 3-1 line (penetrating setter), 2-2 box. Some organizers waive overlap faults (Texas A&M).

5-1.name: 5-1 System (standard)
5-1.description: 1 sole setter distributing across all 6 rotations (3 back-row with penetration + 3 front) + 2 outsides + 2 middles + 1 opposite (diagonally opposite the setter) + 1 libero. The most-used system in elite competition.

P4.description: Main attack zone. The outside receives most high balls and must be versatile: attack, block, reception. Also the left-side off-blocker against an opponent's Z4 attack.

P3.description: Net player in the center zone. Blocks opposing attacks and hits quick tempo. On an opposing wing attack, closes the cross-court with a 2-person block.
traits: Limited defensive role at the net

P2.description: The conductor. Receives the 2nd touch and runs the offense. In 5-1 plays all rotations: penetrates from P1, P6 or P5 (back), distributes from P4, P3 or P2 (front). Target: between Z2 and Z3, ~1 m from the net.

P5.description: Reception and defense zone on the left. Often filled by the 2nd outside in the back-row rotation. The libero may replace them.

P6.description: Defensive pivot at the back. Covers long balls and supports teammates. Often the libero plays here.

P1.description: The opposite ("point hitter") sits diagonally opposite the setter. Does not participate in reception — the finisher. Spends 3 of 6 rotations in the back (attacks from the back — pipe).

L.description: Defensive specialist in a contrasting jersey. Replaces the back-row players (P1, P5, P6) without counting as a substitution. FIVB restrictions: no block, no attack above the net, no overhand set from the front zone to a teammate who then attacks above the net.
traits: Cannot block / attack above the net
No overhand set from front → attacker

4-2.name: 4-2 System (beginner)
4-2.description: 2 setters diagonally opposite (P2 and P5) + 2 middles + 2 outsides. The FRONT setter always takes the 2nd touch. No penetration: the simplest system to learn.

P4.description: Left wing. Setter's main target in zone 4.

P3.description: Front-row middle: block + quick attack when the reception allows it.

P2.description: Front setter: takes the 2nd touch. No penetration, no reception. Distributes from the position.

P5.description: Second setter, diagonally opposite. Plays only as back-row, does NOT take the 2nd touch while back. Receives and defends.

P6.description: Middle going through back-row positions. Center reception + defense.

P1.description: Outside in back-row rotation, serves from P1 then plays reception/defense.

6-2.name: 6-2 System (advanced)
6-2.description: 2 versatile setters: they ONLY set from the back row (with penetration), and become right-side attackers when rotating to the front. + 2 middles + 2 outsides + 1 libero. Pro: always 3 front-row attackers. Con: diluted setter-hitter chemistry, and in the double-sub variant rapidly burns through the 6 substitutions per set (FIVB Rule 15.6).

P4.description: Left wing, main attacker in zone 4.

P2.description: In 6-2 the front-row player (setter or not) attacks. When the setter is front, they become a zone-2 attacker. The back setter distributes.

P5.description: Wing in back-row rotation. Reception and defense.

P6.description: Middle in back-row rotation, often replaced by the libero for reception and defense.

P1.description: Back-row setter who penetrates as soon as the serve is hit toward zone 2-3 to distribute. Facing them, the 2nd setter at P2 attacks.

L.description: Standard libero, replaces middles in the back-row rotation.

pentagon.name: Pentagon (1-2-2)
pentagon.description: 1 player at the center net, 2 wings mid-court, 2 back. Even court coverage — good in beginner and recreational play. Typical defense: 1-2-2 system (adapted man-up, 1 blocker + 2 coverers + 2 deep defenders).

P3.name: Net center
P3.description: At the center net. Often the setter (if fixed); otherwise the primary blocker.

P4.name: Left wing
P4.description: Left wing mid-court: receives and attacks from zone 4.

P2.name: Right wing
P2.description: Right wing. If the setter plays center, this is the zone-2 attacker.

P5.name: Back left
P5.description: Back left: covers the left defense, often the best passer.

P1.name: Back right
P1.description: Back right: covers right defense + serves.

3F-2B.name: 3 front / 2 back
3F-2B.description: 3 attackers at the net (P4, P3, P2 with setter at P2) + 2 back (P5, P1). Offensive setup: 2- or 3-person block possible. Typical defense: 2-1-2 system (2 blockers + 1 off-blocker + 2 deep defenders). Downside: 30+ m² per back-row defender.

P4.name: Left wing
P4.description: Left wing at the net. Main setter target in zone 4.

P3.name: Middle
P3.description: Middle at the net. Block + quick attack when the reception allows it.

P2.name: Front setter
P2.description: Fixed front setter. No penetration. Distributes from the net; can attack in 2 if the ball comes high on the right side.

P5.name: Back left
P5.description: Back left: reception on the left + long cross-court defense.

P1.name: Back right
P1.description: Back right: serves then defends the line and short cross.

2F-3B.name: 2 front / 3 back
2F-3B.description: 2 players at the net + 3 back including the penetrating setter (P1). The most defensively stable setup, closest to 6v6 5-1. Typical defense: 1-1-3 system (1 blocker + 1 off-blocker + 3 deep defenders). Recommended to prepare the transition to 6v6.

P4.name: Left wing
P4.description: Left wing at the net. Main attacker in zone 4.

P3.name: Middle
P3.description: Versatile middle: central block + attack in zone 3 or 2 depending on the set.

P5.name: Back left
P5.description: Back left: reception on the left + long cross-court.

P6.name: Back center
P6.description: Back center: covers the whole back middle, reads long balls.

P1.name: Penetrating setter
P1.description: Back-row setter at P1 who penetrates to zone 2-3 as soon as the serve is hit. Serves then distributes.

losange.name: Diamond (1-2-1)
losange.description: "Diamond" formation: the MOST USED in indoor 4v4. 1 player at the center net (P3, often the setter), 2 wings mid-court (P4 and P2 around the 3 m line), 1 back. Typical defense: A-system (1 blocker + 3 defenders). Most vulnerable zone: long cross-court (lack of bodies in the back).

P3.name: Net center
P3.description: At the center net. Often the SETTER ("center setter" variant) distributing to either side. Otherwise the primary blocker.

P4.name: Left wing
P4.description: Left wing, mid-court (around the 3 m line). Setter's preferred target.

P2.name: Right wing
P2.description: Right wing, mid-court. Attacks in zone 2 if the setter distributes right.

P1.name: Sole back
P1.description: No libero allowed: this is the team's best back defender. Covers the entire back alone.
traits: Must know how to set the 2nd touch

carre.name: Box (2-2)
carre.description: "Box" 2-2 formation: 2 players at the net (P4 and P2) + 2 back (P5 and P1). Enables 2-person blocking (B system) — but only useful against very powerful hitters with no finesse, since it leaves only 2 deep defenders (tip uncovered). More often played in A system with a single blocker.

P4.name: Left wing (net)
P4.description: At the net on the left. Block + attack in zone 4.

P2.name: Setter-attacker (net)
P2.description: Setter-attacker at the net on the right. Always takes the 2nd touch (no penetration in the box).

P5.name: Back left
P5.description: Back left: reception on the left + long cross-court.

P1.name: Back right
P1.description: Back right: serves then defends the line and long cross-court.

3-1.name: 3-1 line (penetrating setter)
3-1.description: "3-1 line" formation: sole setter at P1 (back) who penetrates to zone 2 as soon as the ball is hit. Frees 3 attackers in front — a simplified equivalent of 6v6 5-1. Requires very clean reception and a fast setter. Defense: A system possible (1 central blocker + 3 defenders).

P4.name: Left wing
P4.description: Left wing at the net. Main attacker in zone 4 + reception.

P3.name: Middle
P3.description: Middle at the net. Block + attack in zone 3 if the set is tight.

P2.name: Right wing
P2.description: Right wing. Attacks in zone 2 when the setter distributes right.

P1.name: Penetrating setter
P1.description: Sole setter at P1. Serves then penetrates to zone 2 to distribute.
